messages:
maria: Heads up — v2 routers are falling back to v1 for several tenants in eu-west over the last 30m. Not a total outage but a lot of partial fallbacks. :eyes:
aj: Do we have a single signal? Is it quota exhaustion, model OOMs, or router CPU?
maria: Mostly router-side stats show queue depth spikes and then fallback. I pulled a quick query: `sum(rate(router.requests.fallback[5m])) by (tenant,region)` — eu-west dominated.
tim: Is billing/quotas getting charged against v1 when fallback happens? We should avoid double-charging.
maria: Good catch — currently the router emits `router.request` for the original then `router.fallback.request` for the fallback. Billing pipeline charges on any `request` metric today. That implies double-counting unless we change tagging.
acheng: We should do two things: (1) routing policy to prioritize enterprise tenants when v2 is overwhelmed, and (2) a per-tenant fallback cap so a noisy free-tier tenant can't push enterprise off. Proposed policy sketch:
```yaml
route_policy:
  fallback:
    priority_order: ["sla:enterprise","sla:standard","sla:free"]
    per_tenant_fallback_cap_pct: 10   # max % of tenant's requests that can be routed to fallback in a rolling window
    billing_behavior: "charge_primary_only"
```
aj: +1 on `billing_behavior` default. If we implement `charge_primary_only`, we need the ingestion pipeline to prefer the original model tag when fallback occurs (or emit a single reconciled event). Ops: is that safe for telemetry accuracy?
opsbot: quick note — changing billing tag semantics will affect historical dashboards and queries that rely on model variant tags. Backfill/compat will be needed for any retro reconciliations.
tim: For dashboards we should expose two new panels: `fallback_rate_by_tenant` and `fallback_token_charge_by_tenant`. That will make regressions obvious. Also set an alert: `fallback_rate_by_tenant > 5% for 10m` for enterprise SLAs.
maria: I mocked an alert rule in console: `WHEN sum(router.fallback.count) BY tenant / sum(router.request.count) BY tenant > 0.05 FOR 10m THEN page oncall` — needs a name and proper label joins.
acheng: Implementation notes: router needs to attach `fallback_reason` and `billing_tag_override` when it decides to fallback. Billing pipeline will prefer `billing_tag_override` if present. We'll need a migration plan.
aj: UX: Console should show a per-route toggle to opt into the new `per_tenant_fallback_cap_pct` (default off for now) plus a preview of how many tenants would be affected (simulate using last 7 days).
maria: Agree. Canary plan: enable `billing_behavior: charge_primary_only` and `per_tenant_fallback_cap_pct: 10` for shadow cohort A (10 tenants) for 48h. Observe fallback counts + billing diffs.
deploy-bot: canary-deploy started for router-policy v1.3 to eu-west (cohort A). CI passed: `router-policy-tests` success.
acheng: Post-canary checklist: 1) confirm no double-charges in billing logs; 2) dashboard panels populated; 3) alert thresholds tuned; 4) rollout script to stagger regions.
tim: Also confirm we don't regress latency SLOs for enterprise during the cap enforcement.
amaria: I'll open a short RFC with the policy YAML, telemetry metrics, alert names, and rollout timing. Linking prototype dashboard in the RFC.
aj: Thanks — if anyone can review the RFC today that'd be great. Otherwise we'll schedule a sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary metrics show fallback_count down 43% for cohort A after 15m.
maria: Nice — keep watching. If it holds, we can prep a wider rollout but keep `charge_primary_only` gated until billing confirms.
